text: Marie Curie was a Polish and naturalised French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity. Born in Warsaw, she studied at the University of Paris, where she met her husband Pierre Curie. In 1903 she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel. She later founded the Curie Institute in Paris, and during World War I she developed mobile X-ray units for the French Army. Her daughter Irène Joliot-Curie won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1935.
